newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans end higher on wheat rally, USDA data.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans end higher on wheat rally, USDA data.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures ended higher on Tuesday as wheat rallied and commercials and funds turned strong buyers, traders said.

Soybean futures opened as much as 15 cents per bushel lower as the market reacted to USDA's production estimate of 2.403 billion bushels. That figure was above average trade expectations for 2.376 billion bushels.

But while supply figures were larger than expected, usage numbers were also higher, pointing to continued strong demand, traders said. USDA raised its estimates for export and crush usage by a total of 35 million bushels.
That left ending stocks at 210 million bushels, above last month's levels of 195 million bushels but lower than some analysts had anticipated.
The November contract fell as low as $6.66 a bushel early, just above chart support of $6.65. November peaked at $6.89.

Cargill Inc bought at least five million bushels January and Refco Inc was said to be on both sides of the market, traders said, while Merrill Lynch Futures, Smith Barney and R.J. O'Brien were also said to be buyers.
Soybeans closed 9-1/4 to six cents per bushel higher with November up 8-1/2 at $6.88-1/2 a bushel.
Soybean volume was estimated by the CBOT at 85,000 contracts, well above 33,995 contracts the previous day.
